subject.title: Feature: inbound 'reply in thread' / 'rit' user directive

question: Should OpenClaw reserve natural-language suffixes like `reply in thread` or `rit` as built-in cross-channel reply-routing directives?
rationale: The source-level feature absence is clear, but adding hidden inbound prompt-stripping and reply override semantics creates cross-channel product behavior and possible config surface that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Specify a narrow core directive
options.body: Approve a small suffix contract, likely excluding ambiguous bare `thread`, and require implementation to strip all agent-visible body fields while respecting explicit reply policy.

options.title: Keep it prompt or plugin owned
options.body: Leave natural-language phrasing to prompts or plugins and keep core limited to explicit reply tags, typed commands, and configured reply modes.

options.title: Fold into broader thread routing
options.body: Track the request with the broader thread-placement design if maintainers prefer one policy for suffixes, tool-use routing, and channel-specific threading.

recommendation.title: Specify a narrow core directive
recommendation.body: Approve a small suffix contract, likely excluding ambiguous bare `thread`, and require implementation to strip all agent-visible body fields while respecting explicit reply policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal on the inbound finalizer, reply-threading policy, and directive parser surfaces that would frame the product-shape decision.
